CitationModel.description:
BibTeX model for citations.

https://www.bibtex.com/format/

Includes some non-standard fields.

author.description: The name(s) of the author(s) (in the case of more than one author, separated by `and`).
author.title: Author

url.description: The URL field is used to store the URL of a web page or FTP download. It is a non-standard BibTeX field.
url.title: Url

institution.description: The institution that was involved in the publishing, but not necessarily the publisher.
institution.title: Institution

doi.description: The doi field is used to store the digital object identifier (DOI) of a journal article, conference paper, book chapter or book. It is a non-standard BibTeX field. It's recommended to simply use the DOI, and not a DOI link.
doi.title: Doi

month.description: The month of publication (or, if unpublished, the month of creation). Use three-letter abbreviation.
month.title: Month

year.description: The year of publication (or, if unpublished, the year of creation).
year.title: Year

licence.description: The terms under which the associated resource are licenced for reuse.
licence.title: Licence

CitationModel.title: CitationModel

required.description: Indicates whether a field must have a value for each instance.
required.title: Required

unique.description: When `true`, each value defined by the field `MUST` be unique.
unique.title: Unique

enum.description: The set of unique category terms permitted in this field,  with `name` & (optional) `description`.
enum.title: Enum

default.description: A default category term used when source values are ambiguous, or unstated.

minLength.description: The fewest characters a string may have.
minLength.title: Minlength

maxLength.description: The most characters a string may have.
maxLength.title: Maxlength

ExtensionModel.description:
An action or type a definition uses that whyqd does not include, from the package that provides it.

An extension is known by its package and its name together, since one name in two packages need not do the same
thing. Its version is a range in the Python packaging standard's
[version specifier](https://packaging.python.org/en/latest/specifications/version-specifiers/) syntax, such as
`>=1.2.3,<2`; a transform records the exact version it ran, as `==1.2.3`.

name.description: The action's or type's name, as a definition writes it.
name.title: Name

kind.description: Whether it is an action or a type.

distribution.description: The installed package that provides it.
distribution.title: Distribution

version.description: The versions of that package the definition accepts.
version.title: Version

iri.description: An IRI giving the extension's meaning.
iri.title: Iri

ExtensionModel.title: ExtensionModel

constraints.description: A set of optional constraints to define the field.

policy.description: How to read the field's text as its type.

termList.description: The versioned term list the field's categories come from, taking precedence over `enum`.

NumberFormatModel.description:
How a number is written: the number format of a CSV on the Web derived datatype
([Metadata Vocabulary for Tabular Data, section 5.11.2](https://www.w3.org/TR/tabular-metadata/#derived-datatypes)).

decimalChar.description: The decimal mark, such as `.` or `,`.
decimalChar.title: Decimalchar

groupChar.description: The grouping mark, such as `,` in `1,000`.
groupChar.title: Groupchar

NumberFormatModel.title: NumberFormatModel

PolicyModel.description:
How to read a field's text as its type: a CSV on the Web derived datatype
([Metadata Vocabulary for Tabular Data, section 5.11.2](https://www.w3.org/TR/tabular-metadata/#derived-datatypes)),
`base` and `format`, with whyqd's own `rules` beside it.

A field without a policy is read as text.

base.description: The datatype the text is read as, such as `decimal` or `date`.
base.title: Base

format.description: How the text is written: a number's format; a boolean's `true|false` pair, such as `Y|N`; or a date's pattern, such as `dd.MM.yyyy`.
format.title: Format

rules.description: whyqd's own reading rules, beyond what `base` and `format` say.
rules.title: Rules

PolicyModel.title: PolicyModel

ReasonModel.description:
Why a crosswalk step holds, in the terms of an SSSOM mapping's justification
([SSSOM data model](https://github.com/mapping-commons/sssom/blob/9287d104437ad702fa4e74b1ea2b42a879b877ae/src/docs/spec-model.md)).
It covers every mapping in its step.

The justification is a term from the
[Semantic Mapping Vocabulary](https://mapping-commons.github.io/semantic-mapping-vocabulary/), recording whether a
person or a tool made the judgement: `semapv:ManualMappingCuration` for a wrangler's own, `semapv:MappingReview`
for a check of someone else's.

author.description: Who made the mapping, by name or identifier.
author.title: Author

confidence.description: How sure the author is, from 0 to 1.
confidence.title: Confidence

seeAlso.description: Where more can be read, by URI.
seeAlso.title: Seealso

reference.description: The versioned source the mapping relies on.

ReasonModel.title: ReasonModel

ReferenceModel.description:
A versioned source a definition relies on: a term list, a correspondence, or what a reason cites.

The pair is SSSOM's source and source version (`subject_source`, `subject_source_version`, in the
[SSSOM data model](https://github.com/mapping-commons/sssom/blob/9287d104437ad702fa4e74b1ea2b42a879b877ae/src/docs/spec-model.md)).
The version is required, since a
definition pins what it relies on and never follows a list's current version.

source.description: The source's IRI, or its path where it is private.
source.title: Source

ReferenceModel.title: ReferenceModel
